newsitem.title: POLAND: Hachette given 3 weeks for final Ruch bid.
newsitem.headline: Hachette given 3 weeks for final Ruch bid.

text.p: Polish Privatisation Minister Wieslaw Kaczmarek said on Thursday he had given France's press distributor Hachette a three-week deadline for presenting a final bid for the large state-owned news-stand chain Ruch SA.
"On Tuesday, I decided to grant Hachette the right to be the sole bidder (for Ruch) for three weeks. So negotiations will continue," Kaczmarek told a news conference.

He said that if no deal was clinched during the period, the tender for Ruch, which controls about 65 percent of Poland's press distribution with about 17,000 outlets, could be annulled and a new one launched or a different solution could be sought.
Hachette, leading the consortium involving several Polish firms, wants to buy a strategic stake in Ruch, which netted 16.2 million zlotys on sales of 2.7 billion zlotys in 1995.

An informal group, including Poland's private television station Polsat, mineral water producer Multico and the operator of Poland's lottery, has recently unveiled plans to buy 40 percent of Ruch and offer another 40 percent to the public.
According to newspapers, the group plans to offer $120 million for Ruch and some politicians, opposing the sale of Polish companies to foreign capital, urged Kaczmarek to break talks with Hachette.
Last week, Kaczmarek said he had also received a bid for Ruch from trading company Universal. Universal has declined to give any details on the offer.
